items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to environmental zones
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S428

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the tax law, in relation to
environmental zones

 PURPOSE :

This bill amends the tax law to designate environmental zones based on
data from the 2010 census to ensure that the enhanced brownfield tax
credits are going to projects located in the most economically
distressed areas reflected by the most current economic data.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 amends the tax law to state that the Commissioner of
Economic Development shall use the most recent census data rather than
the 2000 census data when designating environmental zones for any
qualified site which the Department of Environmental Conservation has
issued a notice to the taxpayer on or after July 1, 2015 that its
request for participation has been accepted.

With respect to any qualified site which the Department of
Environmental Conservation has approved between January 1, 2012 and
June 30, 2015, environmental zones shall be designated based on
criteria using data from either the 2000 or most recent census. The
Commissioner shall make such designations and a list of all such
environmental zones before the later of ninety days after the
effective date of the chapter of the laws of 2015 that amended
paragraph 6 of subsection (b) of section 21 of the tax law or ninety
days following the official publication of the most recent census.

Section 2 states that this act shall take effect on July 1, 2015 and
shall apply to any qualified sites for which the Department of
Environmental Conservation has issued a notice to the taxpayer on or
after January 1, 2011 that its request for participation has been
accepted. This section further provides that the provisions of
subparagraph (C) of paragraph (6) of subsection (b) of section 21 of
the tax law shall apply to tax years beginning on and after January 1,
2015

 JUSTIFICATION :

Under New York State's Brownfield Cleanup Program, tax credits are
provided to taxpayers for the cleanup and redevelopment of
contaminated brownfield sites. Additional enhanced tax credits are
provided to taxpayers who rehabilitate contaminated sites that are
located in economically depressed areas designated as environmental
zones. Currently, environmental zones are designated by the
Commissioner of Economic Development if the qualified site meets
criteria based on data from the 2000 census. This bill amends the tax
law to designate environmental zones based on data from the most
recent census. This important change will ensure that enhanced tax
credits are going towards projects that are located in the most
economically distressed areas based on the most recent economic data.

Projects that are accepted into the Brownfield Cleanup Program after
July 1, 2015 will receive the enhanced tax credits only if they are
located in an environmental zone based on the most recent census data.
Projects that were accepted into the Brownfield Cleanup Program
between January 1, 2012 and June 30, 2015 will receive the enhanced
tax credits if they are located in an environmental zone based on
either the most recent census data or data from the 2000 census.
Existing projects that are in an environmental zone pursuant to data
from the 2000 census will continue to receive the enhanced tax
credits.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2013-14: S.7200/A.9711 Passed Senate/Referred to Ways and Means

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect July 1, 2015.
